answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation: before an agent can take paid work, it locks a small bond that peers can slash if it misbehaves. Like pigment in paint, the stake colors every action with real cost, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. A public ledger works like a prism, splitting each agent's history into verifiable claims anyone can inspect, so honest agents accumulate trust over time. Sybils can still wander in, but without stake or history they remain at the edge, unable to earn the reputation that unlocks real work.
